fluff.overview: The Kobold is a light battle armor suit jointly developed by the Free Rasalhague Republic, ComStar, and the second Star League. Entering production in 3069 at Grumium Creations on Grumium, the design was born from the Republic’s desire for a stealth-capable scout suit after failed efforts to procure existing designs from other powers. A humanoid suit with jump capability and low-observable armor, the Kobold filled a gap in Republic and ComStar inventories for a light reconnaissance platform that could hold its own in direct combat while operating alongside heavier battle armor types.
fluff.capabilities: This configuration mounts a micro grenade launcher on each trooper’s modular weapon mount alongside the squad leader’s small pulse laser support weapon. The pulse laser provides accurate energy fire at close range, making this loadout well suited for engagements where ammunition conservation matters or where the squad expects sustained contact. The micro grenade launchers retain their effectiveness against soft targets and clustered infantry. Protected by basic stealth armor rated to withstand a medium laser hit, the Kobold’s light chassis keeps its profile low while armored gloves give troopers the ability to engage BattleMechs directly or ride OmniMechs into combat. The suit’s ninety-meter jump range and 750-kilogram mass strike a balance between the Kage’s pure agility and the heavier armament expected of a frontline-capable design.
fluff.deployment: Ghost Bear garrison clusters that received Kobold suits organized them into standard five-trooper Points. The micro grenade launcher and pulse laser configuration provided Clan warriors with a self-sufficient light scouting element that could sustain operations without the ammunition constraints associated with ballistic loadouts, though most Bears viewed the suits as secondary to their Elemental inventory.
fluff.history:
The Kobold traces its origins to 3062, when the infantry of the Free Rasalhague Republic’s Second Kavalleri sought to acquire Kage battle armor from the Draconis Combine. With tensions rising on all fronts, the Combine refused the request. Överste Jack Koslow, commander of the Second Kavalleri’s attached infantry regiments, continued lobbying his superiors until he received permission to approach ComStar and the second Star League with a proposal for a joint development program. The Republic would supply raw materials while ComStar and the SLDF provided technological expertise, with funding split equally among all three parties.

Research and development began on Grumium, where construction of a prototype manufacturing line was rushed to completion. The design team originally aimed to replicate the Kage’s capabilities but soon shifted focus toward creating a frontline combat suit that retained the Combine design’s reconnaissance strengths. Prototype testing began on schedule in 3065, with the Republic’s Second Kavalleri and ComStar’s 116th Division serving as evaluation units. The SLDF was forced to pull out of the project when ongoing conflicts among League member states cut into its funding. Early problems with the suit’s stealth systems under conditions of high humidity were identified and resolved during testing, and Grumium Creations began full-scale production in 3069.

The KungsArmé adopted the Kobold as the backbone of its battle armor battalions. The Third Drakøns, Second Freemen, Third Hussars, and Second and Fourth Kavalleri all received Kobold-equipped formations. The First Tyr was also reinforced with a battle armor regiment, though its emphasis on direct combat meant it received proportionally fewer Kobolds in favor of heavier suits. In action against Word of Blake forces, the design proved capable against Blakist Purifiers and Phalanxes, earning respect as a light suit that could hold its own in a contested battlespace.

ComStar took a different approach to Kobold deployment. Rather than concentrating the suits into large formations, individual Level Is of six troopers were distributed across Precentor Martial Davion’s reorganized armies. Elements of the First and Fourth Armies deployed on Coventry, Hesperus II, and Galatea grouped light OmniMechs with Kobold-equipped troopers into combined-arms Level IIs, using the suits as scouts and spotters for heavier assets. The deterioration of relations between ComStar and the Republic eventually severed the Com Guards’ access to Grumium’s production lines, limiting their ability to replace losses.

Improving ties between the Republic and Clan Ghost Bear provided limited access to Clan battle armor technology, though the conservative Bears remained suspicious of stealth systems and showed little interest in Inner Sphere equipment. By the mid-3070s, with the second Star League disbanded and the Republic having chosen its Ghost Bear alliance over its ComStar partnership, the Kobold had become firmly a Rasalhague design. The suit earned a rare distinction as one of the few battle armor types fielded by Inner Sphere powers, ComStar, and the Clans alike.
